Description

This PR sits on top of #14665 in the refreshable-token stack. It lets a user make expiring credentials the default without passing `--expiring` on every `gh auth login` and `gh auth refresh`, by adding a `prefer_expiring_credentials` configuration option.

Expiring credentials are OAuth tokens the server issues with a short expiry that gh refreshes automatically on the user's behalf. Until now the only way to prefer them was the `--expiring` flag, which has to be repeated on each login and refresh. A user who always wants expiring credentials had no way to say so once.

The work lands in two commits:

- **`refactor(auth): make --expiring a tri-state *bool flag`** changes `--expiring` on `login` and `refresh` from a plain `bool` to a `*bool` via `cmdutil.NilBoolFlag`. This distinguishes three states that a plain bool collapses into two: flag set to true, flag set to false, and flag unset. An unset flag still behaves exactly as before (no expiring token requested), so this commit carries no behavior change on its own. It also makes `--expiring=false` an explicit, meaningful value, and exports the shared login flow's `authFlow` test seam as `AuthFlow` so command-level tests can stub the interactive authorization and assert whether a refresh token was requested.

- **`feat(auth): add prefer_expiring_credentials config option`** adds the config option itself (`enabled`/`disabled`, default `disabled`). When `--expiring` is unset, the new `shared.ShouldPreferExpiring` resolves the preference from this config for the host; an explicit `--expiring` or `--expiring=false` always wins. So a user can set the config once to prefer expiring credentials, and still request a non-expiring token on a one-off basis with `--expiring=false`.

### How did you test this change?

I built gh from this branch and ran it directly as `./bin/gh`.

I ran `gh config list` and `gh config get prefer_expiring_credentials` and saw the new option registered and resolvable for the host.

I ran `gh auth login --help` and `gh auth refresh --help` and saw the new help text, which explains that enabling `prefer_expiring_credentials` prefers expiring credentials without passing `--expiring`, and that `--expiring=false` requests a non-expiring token even when the config is enabled.

I did not manually drive the full interactive login and refresh OAuth flow for each flag and config combination in this session. The preference resolution is a small, deterministic function (`shared.ShouldPreferExpiring`), and the flag plumbing through login and refresh is exercised by the stack's end-to-end scripts under `script/`.

### Key points

The flag is intentionally split into its own refactor commit so the `*bool` change (which enables distinguishing "unset" from "false") can be reviewed separately from the config option that consumes it.

Precedence is explicit and flag-wins: the flag overrides the config in both directions, so `--expiring=false` disables expiring credentials even when the config enables them. The default is `disabled`, so existing behavior is unchanged for anyone who does not set the config.

### Notes for reviewers

Start at `pkg/cmd/auth/shared/login_flow.go` for `ShouldPreferExpiring`, which is the single resolution point, then see how `login.go` and `refresh.go` call it when the flag is unset. The config option registration lives in `internal/config/config.go` and `internal/gh/gh.go` (with the regenerated mock). `TestShouldPreferExpiring` in `login_flow_test.go` covers all six flag and config combinations.

This PR targets `babakks/refresh-token-rename-flag-to-expiring` (the tip of the stack, #14665), not trunk. Review it after the underlying stack.

Description

This PR sits on top of #14663 in the refreshable-token stack and does one thing: it renames the user-facing `--short-lived` flag to `--expiring` on `gh auth login` and `gh auth refresh`.

The feature lets gh prefer OAuth credentials that the server issues with a short expiry and that gh refreshes automatically on the user's behalf. While wiring up the stack we settled on naming the credential by what it does for the user (it expires, and gh keeps it fresh) rather than by its lifetime. "Expiring" reads more naturally in help text and status output than "short-lived", and it avoids implying anything about how short the window actually is, which is the server's decision.

The rename is mechanical and carries no behavior change. It covers:

- The `--short-lived` flag on `login` and `refresh`, now `--expiring`, including the flag description and the long-form command help.
- The `ShortLived` option fields on the login, refresh, and login-flow option structs, now `Expiring`.
- User-facing strings that tests assert against: the `Received expiring refreshable token` confirmation, the `gh auth status` line `Expiring token that gh refreshes automatically`, the downgrade warning `Original token was expiring; pass --expiring to preserve it`, and the `specify only one of --expiring or --with-token` conflict error.
- Code comments and the two refreshable-token e2e scripts under `script/`.

Where "short-lived" sat next to expiry wording, I dropped the adjective instead of producing redundant phrasing (for example "near-expiry short-lived token" became "near-expiry token"), and I fixed articles ("a short-lived" to "an expiring").

Two unrelated files that use "short-lived" to describe CI GitHub App installation tokens (`docs/release-process-deep-dive.md` and `.github/workflows/shared/dependabot-triage-security.md`) were intentionally left untouched.

### How did you test this change?

Not tested. This is a pure rename of a not-yet-released flag with no behavior change; the renamed user-facing strings are covered by the existing unit tests, and the stack's e2e scripts were updated in step.

### Key points

Pure rename of a not-yet-released flag, so there is no compatibility concern with existing scripts. No logic, storage, or API behavior changes.

### Notes for reviewers

Review can start at `pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go` and `pkg/cmd/auth/refresh/refresh.go` for the flag and help changes, then the user-facing strings in `status.go`, `login_flow.go`, and `refresh.go`. The rest is comment and e2e-script wording. The diff is intentionally symmetric (163 insertions, 163 deletions).

Description

This is a follow-up to the refreshable (short-lived) OAuth token stack (#14450 through #14456). It collects the fixes made in response to review feedback on those PRs into a single branch on top of the stack tip (#14456), so the series history stays readable while the fixes land together.

Because the feedback spanned every PR in the stack, the changes here touch the public HTTP client, the config storage layer, the auth login/refresh/token/status flows, the git credential helper path, agent-task and CAPI per-request refresh, and the guided verification scripts. None of it changes the externally documented behavior of the feature; it corrects edge cases, concurrency safety, and backward compatibility that surfaced during review.

The sections below explain each commit. They are grouped by the PR in the stack that the feedback came from.

### Changes

#### Foundation (#14450)

**`fix(api): keep public HTTP client token config backward compatible`** (9c664a5de)
The exported `api` seam no longer speaks the internal `gh` types. The primitive `config` interface keeps its original shape (`ActiveToken(string) (string, string)` plus `HostForAPIHost`) and `AddAuthTokenHeader` keeps its original signature, so existing downstream consumers compile unchanged. Refresh now lives on a separate, refresh-aware seam: `HTTPClientOptions` gains two mutually exclusive fields, the primitive `Config` and a new `RefreshingConfig`, and the credential and refresh types move to a new public `pkg/auth` package. Regression tests cover the primitive path.

**`test(config): pin intentional active-token lookup behavior`** (1844179a1)
`ActiveToken` has one narrow state that diverges from older gh (per-user config `oauth_token`, no per-user keyring slot, an unkeyed keyring token present, no host-level `oauth_token`). This change keeps the new, more correct behavior as the groundwork for the refreshable per-user slot, adds a code comment explaining why that state is rare in practice, and pins it with a test so it is not later mistaken for a regression.

#### Domain (#14451)

**`fix(config): purge refreshable record on non-refreshable login`** (739aa7253)
A plain `Login` used to leave a stale refreshable record behind, so a user could hold both a refreshable and a non-expiring credential at once. `Login` now removes the user's refreshable record (both keyring and config forms) before completing, mirroring what `loginRefreshable` already does in reverse, so `activateUser` falls through to the non-expiring path and copies the new token into the host-level `oauth_token` slot that go-gh reads for extensions.

**`fix(config): align TokenForUser precedence with setActiveCredential`** (6ea35dd00)
`TokenForUser` now checks the refreshable credential first, then the non-refreshable keyring token, then the non-refreshable config token, matching `setActiveCredential`, so activation and resolution can never disagree about which credential is current even if a mixed state ever slips through. The purge above makes that state unreachable in normal flows, but keeping the order identical is cheap insurance.

#### Login, refresh, and git credential helper (#14452)

**`fix(auth refresh): avoid printing short-lived downgrade warning twice`** (5676a4133)
The post-completion summary no longer repeats the "Original token was short-lived; pass --short-lived to preserve it" line. It is still printed once up front, before the browser prompt, so the user can abort early.

**`fix(auth refresh): preserve scopes when refreshing an expired refreshable token`** (f4f010f59)
With the old `ActiveToken` read, refreshing a credential whose access token had already expired handed back the stale token, so `GetScopes` got a 401 and the refreshed credential came back with no scopes. The refresh now uses `ActiveTokenWithRefresh`, so the token is renewed and persisted first and scopes are read off a live token. When scopes genuinely cannot be read, it prints a non-blocking stderr warning telling the user to re-add scopes with `--scopes` rather than failing the whole refresh.

**`fix(auth/shared): offer to set up gh when a non-gh helper meets a refreshable token`** (4840e2e80)
When the auth flow returns a refreshable token and a non-gh credential helper is configured, gh now explains the problem and offers to set itself up as the helper for the host. Accepting lets gh refresh the token transparently; declining keeps the previous behavior of rejecting the existing credential and warning. This prompt lives at the post-auth setup step because that is the earliest point where both facts are known (the token is refreshable and the helper is non-gh).

**`fix(auth/shared): force web flow for short-lived interactive login`** (669ab0c6f)
A pasted personal access token can never be refreshable, so `--short-lived` now forces the web flow and no longer offers the "Paste an authentication token" choice.

**`fix(auth/shared): clarify warning when declining gh helper setup`** (e47b82d93)
The reject warning now states that the credential was not stored and that git operations may prompt or fail on the next attempt, rather than framing it as a failure only after expiry. This branch is now only reached when the user declines the new setup prompt above.

**`refactor(authflow): extract authResultFromToken for test coverage`** (870382c18)
The mapping from the OAuth flow result to `AuthResult` now lives in `authResultFromToken`, tested directly for both responses: with refresh metadata (refreshable credential populated, expiry anchored at the request instant) and without (plain token, `Refreshable` nil).

#### gh auth token (#14453)

**`refactor(auth/token): drop redundant RefreshStatusDone check under --secure-storage`** (6c1e258e3)
`RefreshStatusDone` is only ever produced after validation that requires a non-empty refresh token, so the credential already satisfies `IsRefreshable()` by then. The `|| refreshStatus == gh.RefreshStatusDone` disjunct was dead code; the condition is simplified to `cred.IsRefreshable()` with no behavior change.

**`fix(auth/token): restore legacy unkeyed keyring lookup when --user is omitted`** (de38197a7)
The non-refreshable keyring fallback was keyed on the resolved active username, so when only the legacy unkeyed keyring slot existed but an active user was recorded, it read the empty per-user slot and reported no token found. It now keys the fallback on the `--user` flag value, so omitting `--user` reads the legacy unkeyed slot exactly as the original `--secure-storage` behavior did. Pinned by two `TestTokenRunSecureStorage` states that fail against the pre-fix code.

#### gh auth status (#14454)

**`fix(auth/status): handle rejected refresh token without an empty-token request`** (f3a64124d)
On a rejected refresh token the credential is removed during resolution, and the old code carried on with an empty token and sent the scope request with `Authorization: token ` (nothing after it), surfacing a confusing generic failure. `buildEntry` now short-circuits on `RefreshStatusExpired`: it skips the scope request, sets a dedicated `refresh_expired` entry state, and prints a clear reason plus the re-authenticate instruction. The entry stays a non-success state, so `gh auth status` still exits non-zero and routes to stderr.

#### agent-task and CAPI (#14455)

**`test(agent-task/capi): assert per-request token refresh in CAPI transport`** (c13b3f42c)
The existing tests supplied a fixed empty credential, so a regression back to a construction-time lookup would have passed unnoticed. A new `client_test.go` exercises the transport directly: one test wires a fake source returning a different token per call and asserts each freshly resolved token becomes that request's header, and another covers the best-effort behavior where the request still proceeds with the last stored token when refresh errors.

**`fix(agent-task): accept plaintext refreshable OAuth credentials`** (dab337767)
The agent-task preflight only recognized the `oauth_token` and `keyring` sources as device-flow logins. A short-lived login whose credential falls back to plaintext config is tagged `refreshable_oauth_token`, so the preflight rejected a supported account before the CAPI refresh path could run. The preflight now accepts the refreshable source alongside the other two.

#### Concurrency safety and robustness (config)

**`fix(config): run logout under the shared refresh lock`** (5c4be83fd)
`Logout` now runs its whole body under the same best-effort refresh lock a concurrent refresh uses, reloading fresh config first, so a logout racing an in-flight refresh cannot be undone by the refresher persisting a renewed credential after the user logged out. Logout wins in both interleavings.

**`fix(config): skip destructive refresh cleanup when the lock is unavailable`** (9f9121e93)
When a refresh token is rejected, the dead credential is normally removed. Without the refresh lock a rejection is ambiguous: a peer process may have already spent the same single-use refresh token and be about to persist the renewed one, so deleting could discard the peer's valid credential. The destructive cleanup is now gated on actually holding the lock; skipping it is self-healing because the next invocation reads the peer's renewed credential.

**`fix(config): don't fail refresh when the config dir can't be created`** (3687fefa4)
Acquiring the refresh lock first ensures the config directory exists. If that creation fails (for example on a read-only filesystem), the refresh now degrades to running without the lock, exactly like a failed lock acquisition, instead of failing outright. The lock is already best effort, and if control reached a refresh the credential was already read, so proceeding is strictly better than erroring. The common case (an existing directory) is unaffected.

**`fix(config): run login under the shared refresh lock`** (24d96ddc5)
`Login` now runs its whole body under the same best-effort refresh lock that `LoginRefreshable` and `Logout` use, reloading fresh config first, so a plain login racing an in-flight refresh wins in both interleavings: a refresh that persists first is superseded by the credential stored here, and a refresh still waiting on the lock reloads afterwards, finds the refreshable record removed, and bails without resurrecting it. The lock stays best effort, so login still proceeds when it cannot be acquired. This commit also surfaces a genuine failure to purge the user's refreshable record during a non-refreshable login: a surviving record outranks the freshly stored token during activation, so a silently failed removal would let login report success while the stale credential stayed active. The check verifies the post-condition by re-reading rather than inspecting the delete error, so it stays silent in environments without a working keyring (an unavailable keyring resolves to not found) and only surfaces when a record provably survives removal.

#### Guided verification scripts (#14456) and housekeeping

**`docs(script): clarify refreshable-token e2e scripts`** (858cab794)
Reworded the script header to describe the scenarios inline instead of linking a note that never shipped, and removed an orphaned `# NEW SYSTEM` banner that had no counterpart.

**`fix(script): declare authtype capability in gitcredential e2e on git 2.46+`** (940a11d97)
Declaring `capability[]=authtype` on git 2.46 and newer makes the `credential fill` steps exercise the same path real fetch and push take, so gh marks the credential ephemeral and the step asserts `ephemeral=1` deterministically instead of leaving it to the eye.

**`docs(script): prompt reviewer to confirm git auth during gitcredential e2e login`** (567cea418)
Added a bold reviewer-action note at the login step so the reviewer knows to confirm the "Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials?" prompt, which exercises the credential-helper setup path for the host.

**`chore: fix formatting`** (f7b5fbd69)
gofmt struct-field alignment in `api/client_test.go` after the longer `RefreshingConfig` field name. No behavior change.

### How did you test this change?

I rebuilt gh from this branch and ran both guided end-to-end verification scripts against a real host, confirming every scenario behaved as expected.

With `script/refreshable-token-e2e.sh` I walked through short-lived login, an ordinary command refreshing an expired token on demand, the `GH_TOKEN` environment path, and `gh auth status` both refreshing and with `--no-refresh`. Refreshes were confirmed from gh's `GH_DEBUG=api` request log and from `auth status` output. I ran this for both the secure keyring theme and the insecure config theme.

With `script/refreshable-token-gitcredential-e2e.sh` I set this build as my git credential helper and exercised resolving a credential, refreshing an expired one through git, and the warning path. My local git is 2.43, so this run exercised the older-git stale-helper warning path rather than the git 2.46 non-cacheable "ephemeral" attribute path.

### Key points

The fixes are kept as focused, individually reviewable commits so each one can be read against the PR it responds to. The single-branch approach was chosen over amending each stacked PR in place to avoid repeatedly rewriting the history of the whole stack during review.

The guided e2e scripts carry testing-only env hacks (for example `GH_AT_EXPIRES_IN`) used to force expiry on demand. These are intentionally retained here so the scripts remain runnable, and will be removed in a dedicated wrap-up PR on top of this one.

### Notes for reviewers

Start from the config storage changes in `internal/config` (`config.go`, `refreshable.go`), which carry the concurrency-safety and robustness fixes, then follow the per-area commits outward into the auth command packages.

This PR targets `babakks/refresh-token-e2e` (the tip of the stack, #14456), not trunk. Review it after the underlying stack.

<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases">releases page</a> for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.</p>
<h2>[UNRELEASED]</h2>
<ul>

<h2>4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li><em>Upcoming breaking change</em>: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4188">#4188</a></li>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.27.2">2.27.2</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4203">#4203</a></li>
<li>Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4184">#4184</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.27.1">2.27.1</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4160">#4160</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4146">#4146</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4124">#4124</a></li>
<li>The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native <code>linux-arm64</code> CodeQL bundle when available. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4072">#4072</a></li>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.27.0">2.27.0</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4129">#4129</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.26.4">2.26.4</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4106">#4106</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026</h2>

</ul>
<h2>4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026</h2>
<ul>

<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases">releases page</a> for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.</p>
<h2>[UNRELEASED]</h2>
<ul>
<li><em>Breaking change</em>: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4205">#4205</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li><em>Upcoming breaking change</em>: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4188">#4188</a></li>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.27.2">2.27.2</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4203">#4203</a></li>
<li>Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4184">#4184</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.27.1">2.27.1</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4160">#4160</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4146">#4146</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4124">#4124</a></li>
<li>The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native <code>linux-arm64</code> CodeQL bundle when available. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4072">#4072</a></li>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.27.0">2.27.0</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4129">#4129</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.26.4">2.26.4</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4106">#4106</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026</h2>
<p>No user facing changes.</p>
<h2>4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Update default CodeQL bundle version to <a href="https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases/tag/codeql-bundle-v2.26.3">2.26.3</a>. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4085">#4085</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to <code>.github/codeql-config.yml</code> to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4070">#4070</a></li>

<h2>4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026</h2>
<ul>
<li>Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the <code>init</code> Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. <a href="https://redirect.github.com/github/codeql-action/pull/4061">#4061</a></li>
</ul>

auth login --with-token` is meant to read a token from stdin. When stdin is a terminal, though, the command blocks on `io.ReadAll` with no prompt or output, so it looks hung (#9789). This happens whenever the flag is used without piping or redirecting input.

**Change.** `NewCmdLogin` now returns a flag error when `--with-token` is set and stdin is a TTY. The message tells the user to supply the token non-interactively, e.g. `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`. Failing fast, rather than prompting or adding a timeout, was the approach suggested in the issue thread. The check runs after the existing `--scopes`/`--with-token` conflict check and before stdin is read. Behaviour is unchanged when stdin is piped or redirected.

In `login_test.go`, the two cases that expected a TTY with `--with-token` to read a token (with and without `--hostname`) now expect an error.

**Verification.** I ran the targeted package, `go test ./pkg/cmd/auth/login`, and it passed, including the updated `Test_NewCmdLogin` cases.

This PR does not change how `--with-token` behaves on a non-TTY stdin that is open but never written to, such as a pipe whose writer never closes. That would need a read timeout or a different input strategy. I can extend the PR to cover it if the maintainers want that.

Fixes #9789

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the

`gh attestation verify` checks an artifact's attestations against the repository or owner passed with `--repo` or `--owner`. By default, the command fetches attestations from the GitHub API, which looks up the repository or owner that currently has that name. With `--bundle` or `--bundle-from-oci`, the command instead reads attestations from a file on disk or from the artifact's OCI registry. In that mode, it compares `--repo` or `--owner` with the repository and owner names recorded in each attestation's signing certificate when the attestation was created.

The help text doesn't describe this difference. Repositories and owners can be renamed, and a different repository or owner can later use the old name, so a name recorded in a certificate doesn't necessarily identify the repository or owner that has that name today.

This PR adds a paragraph to the "Loading Artifacts And Attestations" section of the `gh attestation verify` help text. The paragraph explains that `--bundle` and `--bundle-from-oci` compare names only and can't detect a rename or a reused name. It points users who need that check to the default mode, which fetches attestations from the GitHub API. The [online manual page](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify) is generated from this help text, so it picks up the paragraph in the next release.

I built `bin/gh` from this branch with `make` and built a second binary from `trunk` at this PR's parent commit. I ran `gh attestation verify --help` with each binary and diffed the two outputs. The only difference is the new paragraph, between the `--bundle` paragraph and the "Additional Policy Enforcement" heading:

```diff
--- before (trunk)
+++ after (this branch)
@@ -59,6 +59,15 @@
 For offline verification using attestations stored on disk (c.f. the download command)
 provide a path to the `--bundle` flag.
 
+When you load attestations with `--bundle` or `--bundle-from-oci`, this command
+compares the `--repo` or `--owner` value only with the repository and owner
+names recorded in the attestation's certificate when the attestation was
+created. It cannot detect whether the repository or owner has since been
+renamed, or whether a different repository or owner now uses that name. To
+confirm that an attestation belongs to the repository or owner that currently
+has the name, omit `--bundle` and `--bundle-from-oci` so that this command
+fetches attestations from the GitHub API.
+
 ## Additional Policy Enforcement
 
 Given the `--format=json` flag, upon successful verification this
```

The flag names render in backticks like the surrounding text, and the new lines are at most 79 characters wide. I also ran `go run ./cmd/gen-docs --website --doc-path <temporary directory>` and saw the same paragraph in the "Loading Artifacts And Attestations" section of the generated `gh_attestation_verify.md`.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- This is a help text change only. Verification logic, flags, output, and exit codes are unchanged.
- Making `--bundle` verification check the current repository or owner would need either a GitHub API call, which defeats offline verification, or a new flag for the expected identity. That's a larger behavior change, so this PR documents the current behavior instead.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--

- The change is one paragraph in `pkg/cmd/attestation/verify/verify.go`. To confirm it's accurate, see `getAttestations` in `pkg/cmd/attestation/verify/attestation.go`, which skips the API when `--bundle` or `--bundle-from-oci` is set, and `verifyCertExtensions` in `pkg/cmd/attestation/verification/extensions.go`, which compares `--repo` and `--owner` with the certificate's `SourceRepositoryURI` and `SourceRepositoryOwnerURI`.
- I left the `gh attestation download` help text and the `--bundle` flag description unchanged. Should either of them mention this behavior too?

Fixes #14649

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.

`gh search code` prints each matching line of a code fragment and highlights the matched text. It starts the highlight with an ANSI escape that sets a yellow background, then ends it with a reset escape when it reaches the character at the match's end index.

When a match ends right before a newline, or at the end of the fragment, no character on that line carries the end index. So the reset is never written and the yellow background stays active after the line is printed. If the next newline scrolls the terminal, the terminal fills the new row with the active background, which produces full-width yellow bands.

This PR closes any open highlight at the end of each line and at the end of the fragment. It tracks whether a highlight is open, so a line whose match already ended mid-line does not get a second reset. It also adds colour-enabled tests for `formatMatch`, because none of the existing search code tests enabled colour.

I ran `GH_PAGER=cat gh search code '[cfg_attr(miri, test)]'` twice in the same terminal. The first run used `./bin/gh` built from this branch, and the second used my installed `gh` release.

With this branch (top), each highlight ends after the matched text. With the release build (bottom), the background leaks past the match and fills whole rows once the output scrolls.

![Two runs of gh search code. The top run from this branch highlights only the matched text. The bottom run from the release build shows full-width yellow rows after matches that end at a line break.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74c26801-09d8-4a26-b42d-98be2c861f9c)

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- The reset is only written when a highlight is open. Writing it unconditionally at every line end also works visually, but it adds a redundant escape and stops `strings.TrimSpace` from trimming trailing spaces on the printed line.
- A match that spans a newline is still only highlighted on its first line. The continuation line has no match start, so it is not printed. That is existing behaviour and this PR does not change it.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Start with `formatMatch` in `pkg/cmd/search/code/code.go`, then `TestFormatMatch` in `code_test.go`. The first commit is the original fix from @A4-Tacks, and the second commit narrows the reset and adds the tests.

#14649 has the reproduction steps, including how to put the cursor at the bottom of the terminal so the scroll happens.

### Description

When `gh pr view` (and other `gh pr` commands) is executed with no branch selector argument, it inspects local git branch tracking configuration (`branch.<current>.remote` and `branch.<current>.merge`) to discover the fork remote repository owner and qualifies the head ref as `<owner>:<branch>`. This allows pull requests opened from forks to be resolved properly.

However, passing an unqualified branch name explicitly as an argument (e.g. `gh pr view feature1`) previously treated the branch solely as an unqualified head ref against the base repository, failing with `no pull requests found for branch "feature1"` even when that local branch tracks a fork remote.

This PR aligns the behavior of unqualified branch selector arguments with checked-out branch resolution:
1. When an unqualified branch selector (not containing `:`) is passed to `PRFinder`, it inspects local branch configuration via `PullRequestFindRefsResolver`.
2. If the local branch tracks a remote fork, the head ref is qualified as `<owner>:<branch>`.
3. If the local branch has a merge ref matching `refs/pull/<num>/head` (e.g. checked out via `gh pr checkout`), it resolves the PR by number.
4. If the branch does not exist locally, tracking is unconfigured, or git configuration cannot be read (e.g. outside a repository), it falls back gracefully to the existing unqualified base repository lookup.
5. Explicit `<owner>:<branch>` selectors and numbers continue to bypass local tracking resolution as before.

### Description

Issue artifacts are Markdown documents and links attached to an issue, and this stack adds `gh issue artifact` to work with them. This pull request addresses the review feedback on the stack's first nine pull requests, with one commit per item. Items answered in their thread without a change are listed too.

#### 1/12 #14564: Resolve `--attach` references against the body file's directory

##### Test the drive-relative guard on Windows

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14564#discussion_r4158191167
By: `Copilot` and `babakks`
Commit: 8817625ba7c265b0b00867aca01237184c96ea2b

A test through the lookup can't see this guard, because joining `C:x` onto a folder gives a path like `docs\C:x`, which never matches a real file. So `TestIsRelativePath` tests the guard directly, with Windows-only rows for `C:x`, `\x` and `C:\x`.

##### Share the `--body-file` read

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14564#discussion_r4229508588
By: `babakks`
Commit: c7c38472a725010e96e0ba28a48b78d60d07efcf

`cmdutil.ReadMarkdownBodyFile` reads a `--body-file` and returns its directory, with none for standard input. The six `--attach` commands use it, and so do `gh issue artifact create` and `edit`, through `shared.ReadContent`.

#### 2/12 #14565: Attach one set of files to several Markdown documents

##### Scope `DocumentResult.Err` to the document

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14565#discussion_r4208188646
By: `babakks`
Commit: 0d1d62eacad41203ed19178be1b95bc32c1d1481

The godoc now says the error covers only the document's own attachments, in the suggested wording.

##### Preallocate the failures

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14565#discussion_r4208188679
By: `babakks`
Commit: b6cb86775d89b67f572cc1e4b6e06682cee8add8

`UploadAndAttachDocuments` sizes its failures for the upload error plus one rewrite error per document.

#### 3/12 #14566: Add the command group and `list`

##### Format `--limit` as code

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14566#discussion_r4217513055
By: `babakks`
Commit: d3c13784070b345e866ff23ece44b9d5ae4dca34

`list`'s help puts `--limit` in backticks, like every other flag in the new help.

##### Remove `exportTime`

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14566#discussion_r4217513070
By: `babakks`
Commit: 7129683381b534a78c97acf7ac0a75b75c94fa03

The JSON encoder and gh's exporter already write a nil `*time.Time` as `null`, so the times are assigned directly. The `--json` output doesn't change.

##### Document the last page

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14566#discussion_r4217513077
By: `babakks`
Commit: c4055d1f0f56740b6a5949bca2d4db2f1441f941

A comment in the client's `List` says why stopping at the first short page is safe: the API fills every page but the last.

##### Test the JSON fields with `jsonfieldstest`

Threads: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14566#discussion_r4217513084 + https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474138
By: `babakks`
Commit: 50f6124b5d0063ffc8c967ffb3712e5100fbfc2c

`TestListJSONFields` and `TestViewJSONFields` pin the exact `--json` fields, like `gh discussion list` and `view`. They replace the all-fields rows in `TestNewCmdList` and `TestNewCmdView`.

#### 4/12 #14567: Add `view`

##### Document the order of `versions`

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474086
By: `babakks`

No change. The API returns versions newest first, but there's no way to ask for an order, so `gh` doesn't promise one.

##### Say the current version is shown by default

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474092
By: `babakks`
Commit: 32c8ada6459296340673d2aa6dd2572e2de55c81

`view`'s help says the current version is shown by default. It says "current" rather than "latest" to match the edit history's "Current" label.

##### `--version` with `--web`

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474112
By: `babakks`

No change. Opening an earlier version in the browser isn't supported, on purpose.

##### Show the usage for an invalid argument

Threads: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474117 + https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4229530008 + https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229482450 + https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14570#discussion_r4230280926 + https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14571#discussion_r4230835705
By: `babakks`
Commit: 38787d7aafc92a6e261393de8c6ef752539f9615

An issue or artifact number that doesn't parse is now a flag error in all six artifact commands, so the usage follows the message.

##### A string for `--version`

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474124
By: `babakks`

No change. `--version` stays an integer until there's demand for selectors like `~1`. Switching to a string later keeps plain numbers working.

##### Confirm before `--web` opens a link

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14567#discussion_r4218474133
By: `babakks`

No change. No other `--web` in `gh` asks for confirmation, and `view --web` already opens only an http(s) URL with a host.

#### 5/12 #14568: Add `delete`

##### Real delete responses in the client tests

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4218981007
By: `babakks`
Commit: 577b3b86b970ebe20656d7553c1f90e4d1be0b8f

The stubs return `204 No Content`, or `200` with the deleted artifact's number, and the client accepts both.

##### Whether `deleted` can be false

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4218981013
By: `babakks`

No change. A delete that doesn't happen gets an error status, so the client doesn't need the body.

##### Reword the help

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4229529985
By: `babakks`
Commit: 36eb08f891769ae0aa72924c81a1a1ce79c97f1e

`delete`'s help no longer names `gh`, in the suggested wording.

##### Parallel lookups and deletes

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4229530016
By: `babakks`

No change. It's worth considering as a follow-up.

##### Name the lookup check

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4218981057
By: `babakks`
Commit: 6ea10e3fa9998797e9ccea325272b9d9c02e0993

The lookup failure check is a named variable, `hasLookupFailure`.

##### Report results like other `gh` delete commands

Threads: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4229530021 + https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4229530033
By: `babakks`
Commit: 01d01a44f94a10b5689d187f89d0b350fbc30115

In a terminal, each deleted artifact's line now goes to stderr, like `gh issue delete`. When piped, a deleted artifact prints nothing, and each failure prints `<number>: <reason>` on stderr, like `gh codespace delete`. The `gh` skill describes the new output.

##### Refuse repeated numbers

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14568#discussion_r4229530046
By: `babakks`
Commit: cde6bc91b4ce993674198f8e2b035daa657100ad

`delete` and `download` refuse a repeated artifact number with a usage error, before any request or prompt. Before, `delete 142 2 2` deleted artifact 2 and then reported a 404.

#### 6/12 #14569: Add `download`

##### Mention `--dir` in the help

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229482439
By: `babakks`
Commit: f7f2583e9c6cc8a6dd41acef04c25ce85e80a6d3

The help names `--dir` next to `--output` and `--output -`.

By: `babakks`
Commit: 2f638908e3b3434495ea3170244edd2afc24f957

`--dir ''` wrote every file to the current directory, because a blank directory opens as `.`. It's now a usage error, like a blank `--output`.

By: `babakks`
Commit: d2fd24bbb4d4e88801b256882a12ca8d2f5862a5

`failed = !downloadArtifact(...) || failed` keeps every download running in one line.

By: `babakks`
Commit: 8676746b8c6e036b7c2677794a0bb34e0aeb7f68

A comment says that a name already ending in `.md` or `.url`, in any case, keeps it instead of getting it twice.

By: `babakks`
Commit: febd360b3449ef354efc8a46a9ea863eaef0e3f7

`--output linked`, where `linked` is a symlink to a directory, wrote the file inside it. ##### Test an existing `--dir`

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229423984
By: `babakks`
Commit: 034fa35439456a14530780c46e85afc255427dd9

A new row downloads into a directory that already exists and keeps the file already in it.

##### Remove the `shared` package comment

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229423884
By: `babakks`
Commit: aa344787583ccb3722199cf192a55b26b1a423c9

It listed what the package holds, which changes as commands are added.

##### Default to the only artifact

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229482454
By: `babakks`

No change. It's worth considering as a follow-up.

##### `-O` for `--output`

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229482457

No change. `-O` matches `gh release download`.

By: `babakks`

No change. Like `gh release download` and `gh run download`, `download` fails when there's nothing to download, so a script can't mistake an empty issue for written files.

##### One `List` request for several numbers

Thread: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14569#discussion_r4229423952
By: `babakks`

No change. It's worth considering as a follow-up.

By: `babakks`

No change. Documents are written as stored, and `.url` files use CRLF, as Windows writes them. `create` and `edit` read a shortcut with either line ending.

#### 7/12 #14570: Add `create`

##### Build request bodies from structs

For the first round's changes, I built `gh` at 6ea10e3fa and ran it in a terminal against a new test issue with artifacts 2, 3 and 5. Artifact 9 doesn't exist.

- `gh issue artifact delete <issue> 2 9 --yes` printed `✓ Deleted artifact 2 (OAuth callback plan) from <issue>` and `X Failed to delete artifact 9: Not Found`, and exited 1.
- `delete <issue> 3 --yes 2>/dev/null` printed nothing and exited 0, and artifact 3 was gone.
- `delete <issue> 5 9 --yes | cat` printed only `9: Not Found`, from stderr, and exited 1.
- `delete <issue> 7 7 --yes` and `download <issue> 7 7` each printed `duplicate artifact number: 7` and the usage, and exited 1.
- `view <issue> abc` printed `invalid artifact number: "abc"` and the usage.
- The `list`, `view` and `delete` help showed the new wording.

For the second round's, I built `gh` at e04bc0145 and ran it the same way, in a folder where `linked` is a symlink to the directory `real`:

- `download <issue> 2 --output linked` and `--output linked/` each printed `X Failed to write linked: is a symlink` and exited 1. Nothing was written in `real`.
- `download <issue> 2 --output linked/plan.md` wrote `real/plan.md`.
- `download <issue> 2 --dir ''` printed `` `--dir` cannot be blank `` and the usage.
- `download <issue> 2 5 --dir notes`, with `notes` already holding a file, wrote both artifacts and kept that file. Then `download <issue> 2 --dir notes` printed ``already exists (use `--clobber` to overwrite or `--skip-existing` to skip)``.
- `create <issue> 'plan.md#'` printed ``artifact name after `#` cannot be blank in "plan.md#"`` and the usage.
- `gh issue artifact add` printed `unknown command "add" for "gh issue artifact"`.
- `edit <issue> 3 --body 'not a url'` printed ``artifact 3 is a link; pass an http(s) URL with `--body` or a .url file with `--body-file` `` and exited 1.
- The `create`, `edit` and `download` help matched the updated design.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- **`delete` now prints differently from `create`, `edit` and `download` when piped.** Those keep their five-column lines because they report something a script doesn't have yet: new numbers and file paths. A script already knows the numbers it passed to `delete`.
- **A symlink at `download --output` is refused, even one to a directory.** `--dir` can still be a symlink, as the design says.
- **Three suggestions are kept as they are:** a no-results exit for an empty `download`, usage errors for `--attach` values, and a skill note about errors before any artifact is processed. Each thread says why.
- **`list` and `view` have a third test function.** `jsonfieldstest` is how the repository pins `--json` fields, as in `gh issue view` and `gh pr view`.

Fixes #9789

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`gh auth login --with-token` reads the token from standard input with `io.ReadAll`, which
returns only when the input stream ends. If standard input is the terminal, that end never
arrives: the command prints nothing and waits indefinitely, so it looks like it hung. The
flag's own example, `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`, is the form that works, and
the terminal case is a misuse of the flag rather than a flow the command supports.

This change rejects that case before anything is read. In `NewCmdLogin`'s `RunE`, after the
existing `--web` and `--scopes` exclusivity checks, combining `--with-token` with
`opts.IO.IsStdinTTY()` now returns a `cmdutil.FlagErrorf` naming the piped form. Because it
is a flag error, gh prints the usage block beside it, so the correct invocation is on screen
at the moment the mistake is reported:

```console
$ gh auth login --with-token
argument to `--with-token` must be piped in through standard input, for example `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`

Usage:  gh auth login [flags]

Flags:
  -w, --web                   Open a browser to authenticate
      --with-token            Read token from standard input
  ...
```

Piped and redirected input are unchanged: `io.ReadAll` consumes standard input exactly as
before, including the empty-input case that falls through to the existing non-interactive
path. The two table cases in `Test_NewCmdLogin` that asserted a token could be read from a
terminal now assert the error, and `Test_NewCmdLogin_withTokenStdin` covers the message, the
flag-error type, that the run function is never reached, and both non-terminal shapes.

I built with `make` and ran `bin/gh` from this checkout each time, never an installed gh. For
the terminal cases I allocated a real pseudo-terminal with `/usr/bin/script -q /dev/null`, so
standard input was genuinely a terminal rather than a value I asserted in a test. I isolated
authentication state in a throwaway `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and unset `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`,
so nothing in my existing configuration was read or written.

1. Given the binary from this branch
   When I ran `gh auth login --with-token` with standard input on a terminal
   Then I saw the new error followed by the `gh auth login` usage block, and the process
   exited right away.

2. Given the binary from this branch
   When I ran `printf 'abc123\n' | gh auth login --with-token`
   Then I saw `error validating token: HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/)`,
   which is the unchanged outcome: the token came off the pipe and went to validation.

3. Given a binary I built from trunk with both files reverted
   When I ran `gh auth login --with-token` with standard input on a terminal
   Then I saw no output after 12 seconds and `pgrep` still listed the process, confirming it
   was blocked on standard input. I killed it.

4. Given the binary from this branch
   When I ran `gh auth login --web --with-token` with standard input on a terminal
   Then I saw `specify only one of `--web` or `--with-token``, so the pre-existing conflict
   check still wins over the new one.

I saw no credential written anywhere during these runs: the config file and `hosts.yml` under
my real `~/.config/gh` kept their existing modification times.

One thing I could not provide: the preferred evidence form here is a GIF of the command
running, and VHS, ttyd, and ffmpeg are not installed on this machine, so the observations
above are prose.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- The condition is `IsStdinTTY()`, not `CanPrompt()`. `CanPrompt()` also requires stdout to be
  a terminal, but the block depends on stdin alone: `gh auth login --with-token | tee log`
  leaves a terminal on stdin and still hangs, so keying off stdin catches a case the broader
  helper would miss.
- A flag error, not a plain error, so gh prints the usage block with its examples. This
  matches how the adjacent `--web` and `--scopes` rejections already behave.
- I rejected prompting for the token in the terminal. #9789 states the team does not want
  credential prompts there, and it would reach well past the acceptance criteria.
- Landing order matters here. #14452 adds `if tokenStdin && opts.ShortLived` in the same
  `RunE` block and edits the same test file, so whichever of the two lands second needs a
  rebase. I raise it because it is a review-ordering question a reviewer would otherwise have
  to discover, not because this diff depends on that one.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--

Start with the six added lines in `NewCmdLogin` in `pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go`; the rest of
the diff is tests.

- #9789 carries the acceptance criteria this implements, including the framing that the fix is
  an error rather than an added prompt.
- #14452 touches the same statements in the same function and the same test file, which is why
  it appears under Key points.

<blockquote>
<h2>v0.1.16</h2>
<h2>Improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>Reduce parsing overhead and allocations for Windows consoles without VT support by processing text and escape sequences directly from input slices.</li>
<li>Avoid redundant console queries and attribute resets, and reduce Windows API argument allocations.</li>
<li>Precompute the 256-color mapping, removing first-use conversion work and concurrent initialization races.</li>
<li>Speed up ANSI sequence stripping in <code>NonColorable</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Add regression coverage for fragmented sequences, Unicode titles, palette conversion, and real Windows console operations. CI passes on Windows, macOS, and Linux with Go 1.24, 1.25, and 1.26.</p>
<p>Implemented in <a href="https://redirect.github.com/mattn/go-colorable/issues/84">#84</a>. Real console output remains limited by console I/O: local benchmarks showed about 29% higher throughput for 4 KiB text with an escape sequence and about 3% for colored log lines; parser-only gains are substantially larger.</p>
<p><strong>Full Changelog</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/mattn/go-colorable/compare/v0.1.15...v0.1.16">https://github.com/mattn/go-colorable/compare/v0.1.15...v0.1.16</a></p>
